additionalCoursework: Creighton University School of Medicine has no defined prerequisite course requirements. However, as preparatory to the MCAT and a rigorous medical school curriculum, we recommend the following recent (past 3 years) coursework in an accredited 4-year college/university in the United States or Canada: Strong background in biology including introductory and advanced courses, e.g., physiology, immunology, and genetics. Strong background in chemistry including introductory and advanced courses, e.g., biochemistry. Additionally, coursework in English, humanities and statistics is strongly recommended. Minimum total coursework credits in biology, chemistry, physics, and math should be 40-45 hours.

medSchoolStudLife.diversity: Qualified candidates from populations underrepresented in medicine are encouraged to apply. Creighton's Office of Health Sciences Multicultural and Community Affairs has several active programs to increase diversity and provide support services. The office administers several diversity programs, including pathway and a premedical post baccalaureate program.
medSchoolStudLife.leaveOfAbsence: A student is granted a leave of absence when a temporary interruption of his/her academic schedule is in the best interest of the student or the School of Medicine.  A leave of absence is not granted for longer than two years.
medSchoolStudLife.organizationActivities: Students have the opportunity to be involved in various organizations and activities that enhance the medical school experience both on campus and within the community.
medSchoolStudLife.setting: The first campus is located is near Omaha's vibrant downtown, the entertainment and business center of the city, on Creighton University's 130-acre campus. The Creighton Phoenix Health Sciences Campus is located in the heart of Phoenix with close proximity to all of the up-and-coming and local favorite neighborhoods and their establishments.
medSchoolStudLife.housing: In Omaha, many students find safe and charming apartments in renovated historic buildings close to Creighton and Omaha's Old Market. In Phoenix, there are abundant secure and alluring housing options in the neighborhoods in close proximity to both the health sciences campus and clinical sites. There is limited graduate housing available on campus in Omaha and none in Phoenix.
medSchoolStudLife.supportSystems: We have several student organizations that focus on supporting gender and sexual minority students.  Justice in Medicine, whose main functions is to educate ourselves and the rest of the medical school on important justice issues and establish connections. Health Together is Creighton's Allied Health Professions Queer-Straight Alliance. Medicine Gender and Sexuality Alliance aims to Bring attention to the issues that LGBTQIA people face as patients and/or healthcare providers. Med GSA wishes to establish a safe space for LGBTQIA individuals and to educate about LGBTQIA terminology and inclusivity.
medSchoolStudLife.supportSystemsForDisabilities:
Office of Disability Accommodations – Coordinates academic, clinical, and testing accommodations for students with documented disabilities.
Individualized Accommodation Plans – Adjustments such as extended exam time, assistive technology, note-taking support, or modified clinical schedules when appropriate.
Confidential Advising – Staff who guide students through documentation, requests, and ongoing support.
Wellness & Counseling Services – Mental health support, stress management resources, and referrals.
medSchoolStudLife.wellnessPrograms:
The School of Medicine is committed to supporting every aspect of your medical school journey, which includes a well-rounded approach to your personal well-being and development. You’ll find this support woven into your education and mentoring, along with the following programs and resources.

The Physician Lifestyle Management Course is a one-credit course created to focus on the developing physician. Through each stage of their medical education, students will have opportunities to develop in multiple areas. This course provides opportunities for self-knowledge and growth. 

Medical students tend to become consumed by their academic challenges. Part of being a successful student and developing a fulfilling career is learning to manage stress and maintain a balanced lifestyle. Wellness lectures, newsletters, and activities on topics such as stress management, mood and anxiety are provided for students throughout the year. Activities such as picnics and ice skating are sponsored by the school to enhance balance, well-being and class camaraderie.
medSchoolStudLife.campusCulture: Creighton University emphasizes cura personalis, or care for the whole person, not just as a physician but as an individual. This mission instills a sense of social responsibility, ethical practice, and service to undeserved populations. Students are encouraged to see medicine as a calling that involves empathy, integrity, and care for both patients and society. Students and faculty at Creighton work closely together in a supportive, teamwork-oriented environment. The culture promotes collaboration rather than competition, with a focus on helping each other succeed. This is reflected in study groups, team-based learning, and peer mentoring. We offer resources to support student well-being, including counseling services, wellness programs, and peer support systems. The school fosters a culture of caring for students' mental and physical health, which is essential for their success both academically and in their future medical careers.
medSchoolStudLife.transportationAdditionalInfo: Students will be expected to travel to various clinical sites beginning in the M1 year.

medSchoolCurriculum.patientInteraction: Students began interacting with patients within their first semester of medical school. This expands as they progress through their medical school curriculum.

medSchoolCurriculum.curricularHighlights: The Experience.Reflection.Action. (ERA) curriculum takes a blocked schedule systems approach to human biology and fully integrates basic sciences with clinical science applied in the practice and the art of medicine. The ERA Curriculum is based on Ignatian pedagogy that encourages students to engage in a constant process of ongoing critical self-reflection. The interactive learning environment features team-based learning, larger lectures, small group activities, early clinical activities and self-directed learning. Year three is organized into seven clerkships and three electives within six 8-week rotation periods. The fourth year prepares students for residency and provides a chance to explore their own interests in specialized areas of medical practice.  Ethical and societal issues are prominent in the curriculum in each year.  Students are graded based on curriculum standards and earn either honors, pass or fail scores.
medSchoolCurriculum.primaryCarePrograms:
Creighton emphasizes the importance of primary care in serving underserved populations and improving healthcare access. Creighton’s curriculum is designed to provide students with a solid foundation in primary care principles, including patient-centered care, preventative health, and community-based medicine. Through service learning, clinical rotations, and partnerships with local and regional healthcare providers, students gain firsthand experience working in primary care settings and addressing health disparities.

Additionally, Creighton’s medical school offers programs and initiatives that support students interested in primary care careers, such as mentoring, research opportunities, and exposure to rural and urban underserved communities. Many Creighton graduates go on to practice primary care, particularly in underserved areas, contributing to the school’s mission of promoting health equity.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchPrograms: Students have the opportunity to participate in Creighton's Summer Research Fellowship Program the summer after their first year.  Students will propose and complete a research experience within the basic or clinical sciences, and complete the project under the supervision of a research mentor.  Additional research opportunities are available throughout the curriculum.
medSchoolCurriculum.communityServiceText: Not required, however, 100% of our students participate in community service prior to graduation.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchThesisText: Students may complete directed independent research in the summer after M1 year.
medSchoolCurriculum.affiliatedHospitals: Creighton University’s primary clinical partner in Omaha is CHI Health.  For our Phoenix campus, we partner with Dignity Health St. Joseph’s Hospital and Medical Center and ValleyWise Health.

medSchoolInformation.generalInformation: Creighton University School of Medicine, rooted in Jesuit values, emphasizes the development of compassionate, ethical physicians committed to service and excellence. Its holistic admissions process seeks students with strong academic records and a passion for service, diversity, and community engagement. The curriculum blends scientific rigor with humanistic care, promoting cultural competence, empathy, and ethical decision-making. Students engage in service learning, community outreach, and clinical experiences, with a focus on underserved populations. Creighton’s supportive student life offers wellness resources, mentorship, and personal development opportunities. Graduates, inspired by the school’s mission, excel in primary care and leadership roles, advocating for healthcare equity and serving communities in need, both locally and globally. We have two separate four year campuses. One in  Omaha, Nebraska and one in Phoenix, Arizona.
medSchoolInformation.missionStatement:
Creighton University School of Medicine’s mission focuses on the values of service, integrity, and excellence in medical education, all grounded in Jesuit traditions. This mission guides various aspects of the school, from recruitment and admissions to curriculum design and student life, ultimately shaping the professional identity of graduates. 
Creighton’s mission emphasizes the development of compassionate, ethical, and service-oriented physicians. As such, the admissions process is designed to prioritize candidates who demonstrate a commitment to service, social responsibility, and alignment with the school’s Jesuit values. The school values diversity and seeks applicants who are not only academically accomplished but also possess the qualities of empathy, integrity, and a passion for helping others. This results in a holistic admissions process that evaluates academic performance, life experiences, leadership, and an applicant’s desire to engage in the community and serve the underserved. This approach attracts students who are aligned with the mission of serving others, particularly in under-resourced communities.
The curriculum at Creighton University School of Medicine is rooted in the Jesuit values of cura personalis (care for the whole person), service to others, and ethical practice. The content and structure of the curriculum reflect a balance between the scientific and humanistic aspects of medicine. The school incorporates service learning, community outreach, and clinical experiences that emphasize empathy, cultural competence, and patient-centered care. Students engage in hands-on opportunities to serve in local and global health initiatives, with the goal of cultivating physicians who are not only skilled but also compassionate and socially conscious. Additionally, the curriculum encourages critical thinking and ethical decision-making, fostering future leaders who will advocate for healthcare improvements and social justice.
The Jesuit mission of Creighton places a strong emphasis on the development of students as individuals who are prepared to serve society and lead ethically. Student life is shaped by the school’s commitment to holistic development, providing a supportive environment for students to grow academically, emotionally, and spiritually. Students are encouraged to engage in service activities, reflection, and personal development programs. The school offers counseling, mentorship, and wellness resources to support students' well-being and academic success. There is a strong sense of community within the student body, with collaborative learning and a focus on building relationships that reflect the values of empathy, respect, and care for others. Additionally, support services such as career counseling, faculty mentorship, and access to healthcare resources help students navigate the challenges of medical school while maintaining a balance between personal and academic growth.

Graduates of Creighton University School of Medicine carry forward the mission of the institution in their professional lives, contributing to healthcare in ways that are grounded in ethical practice, compassionate care, and a commitment to underserved populations. Many Creighton graduates pursue careers in primary care, family medicine, and specialties that serve disadvantaged communities. They are trained to approach their patients as whole individuals, with respect for their unique experiences, cultural backgrounds, and needs. Many also take on leadership roles in healthcare systems, advocacy, and public health, working to improve access to care and reduce health disparities. The values instilled at Creighton also lead graduates to serve in international settings, offering their skills and knowledge to underserved populations around the world. Overall, the mission of Creighton’s School of Medicine fosters graduates who are not only skilled clinicians but also compassionate and socially responsible leaders in healthcare.

medSchoolApplication.cbcRequired: Yes. We utilize the service selected by the AAMC and all accepted students must complete the background check prior to matriculation

medSchoolApplication.amcasLettersText: Applicants must submit between three and six letters of recommendation. If their premedical advising office provides a committee letter that compiles feedback from multiple letter writers, it will meet our requirements. All letters must be signed or on official letterhead and submitted through the AMCAS Letters of Evaluation/Recommendation service.
medSchoolApplication.letterGuidance: You may use your discretion when selecting letter-writers. A committee letter is preferred (if available), but not required. We prefer letters from individuals who can honestly and accurately attest to your performance, character, personal qualities, and aptitudes from direct knowledge, interactions, and observations. We suggest you provide us with two science faculty letters and one non-science faculty letter, but leave it up to you to determine who are the ideal persons to help us assess your candidacy for medical school.
medSchoolApplication.typicalInterviewDay: The Interview Program is designed for the Admissions Committee and applicants to learn about each other. medSchoolApplication.interviewFormat: All interviews will be conducted virtually with two open-file one-on-one interviews with a faculty/staff member and a current student during the week and a live Friday wrap up session. We will also host multiple in person admitted student days.

medSchoolApplication.letterOfIntentAdditionalInfo:
It is vitally important that you keep us updated with information that is pertinent to your application throughout this upcoming cycle. Updates should include information that is in addition to, and/or, clarifies information within your AMCAS application. Updates not only allow the Admissions Committee to evaluate your application with the most recent information available, but also demonstrates your interest in continuing to seek admission to CUSOM.  We especially encourage updates that pertain to the following: 
•Clinical experiences 
•Non-medical community service experiences 
•Grades through unofficial/or official transcripts 
•Honors or awards 
•Research

You are able to submit updates through the Secondary Application Portal.
medSchoolApplication.technicalStandardInfo:
In evaluating applicants for admission and in preparing candidates for the M.D. degree, it is essential that the integrity of the curriculum be maintained. That those elements deemed necessary for the education of a physician be preserved and that the health and safety of
patients be maintained. While reasonable accommodation can be made for certain disabilities on the part of the student or candidate, those candidates and students who are disabled will be held to the same fundamental standards as their non-disabled peers.
The Creighton University School of Medicine will consider for admission any candidate who demonstrates the ability to perform the skills and abilities specified in these technical standards with or without reasonable accommodation consistent with the Americans with Disabilities Act.

medSchoolSelection.premedReqRec:
Creighton University School of Medicine has no defined prerequisite course requirements. However, as preparatory to the MCAT and a rigorous medical school curriculum, we recommend the following recent (past 3 years) coursework in an accredited 4-year college/university in the United States or Canada: Strong background in biology including introductory and advanced courses, e.g., physiology, immunology, and genetics. Strong background in chemistry including introductory and advanced courses, e.g., biochemistry. Additionally, coursework in English, humanities and statistics is strongly recommended. Minimum total coursework credits in biology, chemistry, physics, and math should be 40-45 hours.

The Committee on Admissions requires applicants to have a foundation in the following activities:
Commitment to “service of others” through non-medical volunteer activities 
Diverse physician shadowing experiences 
Patient contact through clinical and/or medical experiences
medSchoolSelection.oldestPrereqDate: Creighton University School of Medicine has no defined prerequisite course requirements.
medSchoolSelection.selectionFactors: The qualities of intellectual ability and curiosity, emotional maturity, honesty, proper motivation, proven scholastic ability, significant service to humanity, physician shadowing, and documented medical experience are of highest importance. Both the AMCAS and Creighton secondary applications are required of all applicants. A formal interview on campus is conducted prior to acceptance. No restrictions are placed on applicants due to race, religion, sex, national or ethnic origin, age, disability, veteran status, or state of residence. Creighton values diversity in its medical classes. Applicants who complete their pre-professional education at Creighton are given preference for admission.
medSchoolSelection.preMedShadowText: We value diverse clinical experiences, including exposure to physician shadowing. The goal is that the applicant obtain enough experience to have formulated a decision to pursue medicine, understand the field of medicine, interact with patients, and understand the role of a phycisian.
